hypothesis: In measured NHANES stature by age for boys, the annual height increment is largest in infancy, falls to a long, nearly constant plateau at ages ~4-9, rises again to a second peak in the early teens (~11-15), and then drops to near zero by ages 17-19.
pass_criterion: Using survey-weighted median stature (recumbent length under 2 years, standing height from 2 years) for boys, pooled across NHANES cycles and binned by age, compute annualized increments. All four conditions must hold. (1) Infancy: the mean annualized increment from ages 2-5 months to 18-23 months is at least 1.5 times the mean annual increment across ages 5-9. (2) Steady childhood: each annual increment from age 4 to age 10 lies between 4.0 and 7.5 cm/yr, and their coefficient of variation is 20% or less. (3) Teen quickening: the maximum annual increment at ages 10-15 is at least 1.25 times the mean childhood increment at ages 5-9, and the peak age falls in 11-15. (4) Arrest: the mean annual increment at ages 17-19 is below 1.0 cm/yr and below 25% of the childhood mean.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if any one of the four conditions is violated. Examples: the infancy increment is less than 1.5 times the childhood mean; childhood increments fall outside 4.0-7.5 cm/yr or have a CV above 20%; no teen increment reaches 1.25 times the childhood mean, or the peak falls outside ages 11-15; or the 17-19 increment is 1.0 cm/yr or more.
interpretation: Thompson's 'length or stature in man' is read as measured recumbent length (under 2 years) and standing height (2 years and over). 'Rapid increase at the outset' is read as the annualized growth rate in the first two years. 'Almost steady growth in early boyhood' is read as ages ~4-9. 'Marked quickening in the teens' is read as the adolescent growth spurt, a second maximum in velocity in boys. 'Gradual arrest' is read as velocity near zero by the late teens. Thompson's curves were longitudinal. NHANES is cross-sectional, so velocity is inferred from differences between successive age-bin medians, which is a modern reinterpretation. Birth to 2 months is not covered, so infancy is tested from 2 months. The claim is tested for boys, as stated. Girls could serve as a secondary check.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) – Body Measures (BMX) and Infant/Child examination data
dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES records measured, not self-reported, stature. The BMX files give BMXHT (standing height, cm) and BMXRECUM (recumbent length, cm, for infants and toddlers). The demographics files give RIDAGEYR and RIDAGEMN (age) and RIAGENDR (sex), and the examination weights (WTMEC) are used for survey-weighted medians. The files are freely downloadable as XPT, so pooling cycles gives enough boys per age bin to estimate medians from infancy to age 19.
